note: Friday 6 Nov 2026 07:02 SGT run, pre-Asia-open / post-Thursday-US-close. The dominant story flipped overnight: Wednesday's huge post-midterm relief rally (VIX -20.3%, Dow +3.03%) reversed violently on Thursday (S&P -4.36%, Nasdaq -5.52% into correction, VIX +69.7% to 28.18) on an AI-capex political-risk shock, not fresh macro data. 6 of 14 items are from the last 24 hours (Nov 5-6) and the rest from Nov 4-5.

items.headline: US stocks post biggest selloff of the year as AI-capex political-risk fears erase the entire post-midterm relief rally
items.summary: S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353.73, Nasdaq dropped 5.52% to 24,315.00 (correction territory) and VIX spiked 69.7% to 28.18 -- its biggest one-day jump this year -- after Texas's governor-elect campaigned on pausing new AI data-center construction in the largest US data-center market. UBS estimated up to a third of projected 2028 capacity could be delayed; debt-financed 'neocloud' names were hit hardest (CoreWeave -14.3%). AMD beat and raised guidance yet still fell ~15%, confirming the move was a sentiment/policy repricing rather than an earnings problem.
items.actionable: This directly reverses Wednesday's risk-on tailwind and argues for caution into today's NFP print; the portfolio has no direct AI-hardware exposure but the broad ~6:1 negative NYSE breadth means little was spared, including the levered-silver and HK-tech sleeves.

items.headline: HK tech rallies hard as investors rotate OUT of AI hardware/chips and INTO China internet platforms
items.summary: Hang Seng Tech Index jumped 5-5.5% as Tencent (+7.17% to HK$430.40), Xiaomi (+8.83% to HK$31.30) and SMIC (+2.28% to HK$47.50) rallied while US and Korean semiconductor names sold off on the same AI-regulation fears. Bloomberg frames this as a rotation trade -- investors moving from AI hardware/data-center plays into Chinese internet platforms seen as safer AI-monetization beneficiaries -- rather than a China-specific policy catalyst.
items.actionable: The rally is real but Southbound Stock Connect data (below) shows mainland money sold INTO this strength rather than chasing it -- a durability flag for the HK tech leg of this book rather than a clean all-clear.

items.headline: Southbound Stock Connect sees largest outflow in 7 months (-HK$21.3bn) even as HK tech rallies -- mainland investors took profit, didn't chase
items.summary: Mainland investors sold a net HK$21.33bn of HK stocks on Nov 5, the largest single-day Southbound outflow since April, even as the Hang Seng Tech Index posted its best day in months. Xiaomi alone saw the largest single-stock outflow (HK$3.17bn); index ETFs (Tracker Fund, CSOP Hang Seng TECH, HSCEI) absorbed most of the selling.
items.actionable: Profit-taking by the market's most conviction-driven participant into a rally is a caution flag, not a confirmation, for the owner's 0700/0981/1810 exposure -- watch whether Southbound flow turns net positive again before reading Thursday's price strength as durable.

items.headline: Korea's KOSPI plunges 5.28% as the Nasdaq's AI-capex selloff spreads directly into Samsung and SK hynix
items.summary: KOSPI fell 5.28% to 5,383.80, triggering an intraday circuit-breaker-level move, as foreign investors sold a net ~₩3.4 trillion (~US$2.53bn) concentrated in Samsung Electronics and SK hynix on the same US AI-capex-regulation fears hitting Wall Street. Retail (+₩2.28tn) and domestic institutions (+₩848.5bn) bought the dip but could not fully offset the foreign selling.
items.actionable: Confirms the AI-capex scare is a genuine regional semiconductor-sector event, not a US-only story -- relevant context for reading SMIC's relative resilience (+2.28%) as a China-specific divergence from the Korea-chip selloff rather than the sector moving as one block.

items.headline: Oil reverses Wednesday's crash as fresh Strait of Hormuz tanker incidents reignite Iran-war risk premium
items.summary: Brent/WTI proxies rose ~3-5% Thursday, clawing back part of Wednesday's 8%+ crash, after Iran's IRGC reportedly set tankers and a tug ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz -- the fifth such incident since Sunday, matching October's record pace -- and Saudi Arabia warned of fresh Houthi threats to the Yanbu Red Sea hub. Citi flagged risk of executive-branch Iran-strike escalation regardless of the new Democratic Congress.
items.actionable: No direct oil holdings, but the within-48-hour double reversal (-8% then +5%) shows the Hormuz risk premium never actually resolved, just got mispriced for one session -- a genuinely two-sided, headline-driven market to flag for the macro backdrop rather than a confirmed trend either way.

items.headline: Silver and miners underperform gold as a high-beta spillover from the tech selloff, not a metals-specific event
items.summary: Gold held its post-election safe-haven bid (GLD +0.81%) while silver slipped (SLV -0.49%) and the miners fell harder (SILJ -1.64%, HL -3.34%, PAAS -2.19%) on Nov 5. Kitco's PM wrap attributes this to silver's dual industrial-metal exposure amplifying beta to the Nasdaq-led selloff -- no COMEX margin change or SLV outflow was found; SLV actually saw net weekly inflows.
items.actionable: This is a beta story, not a reversal of the silver thesis -- the levered-silver sleeve's underperformance Thursday tracked the broad equity rout rather than signaling fresh metals-specific weakness; today's NFP is the next real test.

items.headline: Rare-earth basket diverges sharply: Lynas +8% on its own record quarterly update while MP (-6%) and Energy Fuels (-8%) fall on US-truce and earnings-miss reasons
items.summary: Lynas (LYC.AX) jumped 8.01% on an ASX quarterly showing gross sales revenue +55% q/q to A$310.1m and a record average selling price of A$102.1/kg. MP Materials fell 6.04% ahead of its own Q3 print (which beat after the close) as the extended US-China trade truce reduced the near-term supply-crunch premium and reports surfaced the US may step back from planned critical-minerals price floors. Energy Fuels fell 8.22% after missing Q3 estimates (a $52.4m net loss) and an HC Wainwright price-target cut to $22.50.
items.actionable: Clean divergence between a company-specific beat (Lynas) and policy/earnings-driven weakness (MP, Energy Fuels) -- the ex-China basket is not trading as one block right now, which matters for sizing any single name versus the REMX basket.

items.headline: China's rare-earth export-control suspension expires Nov 10 with no formal MOFCOM renewal notice yet
items.summary: China's November 2025 suspension of its expanded rare-earth export controls (the 0.1% de-minimis rule) lapses Nov 10, 2026, and as of Nov 5 Beijing has issued no formal renewal notice despite the broader US-China trade truce having been extended to Jan 10, 2027 in September. The April 2025 licensing regime on seven medium/heavy rare earths was never suspended and stays in force regardless of what happens Nov 10.
items.actionable: The Nov 10 deadline is genuinely live and unresolved -- watch for whether Beijing publishes matching legal text; a lapse would revive the supply-crunch premium that has been driving MP/UUUU, while a quiet extension would extend Thursday's de-rating.

items.headline: PBOC steps up market-backstop measures: cuts stock-buyback relending rate, raises FX reserve requirement to 6% effective Nov 15
items.summary: The PBOC launched a daily overnight reverse-repo facility as its new policy anchor (¥541bn at 1.25% on Nov 2), cut the relending rate for stock buybacks 25bp to 1% and made it a standing facility (bank quota requests already exceeding ¥200bn/~$30bn), ran a third Securities/Funds/Insurance Swap Facility operation, and will raise the FX reserve requirement ratio from 4% to 6% from Nov 15 to stabilize the yuan.
items.actionable: A meaningful policy-support signal for China/HK equities broadly, but it predates and is separate from Thursday's AI-rotation-driven HK tech rally -- read as a floor-under-the-market factor rather than the rally's direct cause.

items.headline: US October nonfarm payrolls due today 21:30 SGT, consensus 65K after September's steep 29K miss -- the key swing catalyst
items.summary: The BLS October jobs report is due at 8:30am ET (21:30 SGT) Friday Nov 6, with consensus around 65K (vs September's 29K miss) and the unemployment rate expected to hold at 4.2%. Average hourly earnings m/m consensus is 0.3% (vs 0.1% prior). This lands the day after the AI-capex-driven selloff and hawkish Fed speak pushed December-hike odds to roughly 68-73%.
items.actionable: The single most important scheduled data point for this portfolio today -- a soft print could revive rate-cut hope and lift both equities and gold/silver; a hot print into an already-hawkish Fed risks extending Thursday's selloff and pressuring the metals complex via higher real rates.

items.headline: A fourth possible government shutdown looms as the CR expires Dec 11 and lame-duck Congress returns Nov 9 with no appropriations progress
items.summary: The current continuing resolution funding the US government expires December 11, 2026. Congress returns from recess November 9 for a lame-duck session, and as of this week there is no visible appropriations progress, raising the prospect of a fourth possible shutdown of the current Congress's term.
items.actionable: An unresolved tail risk sitting underneath the AI-capex/Fed story -- worth tracking into late November as Congress's return date approaches, since a shutdown fight landing on top of an already-hawkish Fed would compound volatility rather than offset it.
